newsitem.title: BELGIUM: AXA Belgium public bid to start Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: AXA Belgium public bid to start Nov 4.

text.p: French insurance group AXA SA said on Wednesday that its public bid in the form of a share swap for the remaining 5.23 percent of shares in its main Belgian unit would run from November 4 to 26.
AXA will offer three of its own shares, entitled to a dividend as of January 1996, for every two held in Brussels-listed AXA Belgium. The AXA shares are dematerialised.
"This gives shareholders a premium of about 50 percent on the stock's price before the announcement of the bid (on October 7)," AXA Belgium chief executive Patrick de Courcel said.
AXA SA said it would also take up the swap costs.
"The small shareholder is being well treated," de Courcel told a news conference.
Shares in AXA Belgium, AXA's main unit in Belgium, were down 10 francs at 2,890 on the Brussels bourse on Wednesday against 1,870 francs just before the news of the swap.
AXA Belgium will be delisted from the Brussels stock market following the operation, which has been approved by Belgium's bourse regulator.

The delisting effectively ends months of speculation about the future of AXA Belgium, which was the French group's only listing outside Paris and New York. A listing in Brussels of AXA SA stock will not be requested.
De Courcel said AXA wanted to avoid a fragmentation of bourse listings but stressed the delisting did not mean that the French group had plans to withdraw from the Belgian market.
He said the free float of capital had nearly halved since AXA Belgium was first listed a decade ago and now totalled 356,815 ordinary shares.
De Courcel said the swap with AXA SA stock offered AXA Belgium shareholders the advantage of improved liquidity and AXA's wider scope of activities and prospect of expansion.
The delisting would also help reduce costs, he added.
De Courcel said no attempt will be made to buy out shareholders who refused to accept the offer.

AXA Belgium, which forms the AXA Group in Belgium with De Kortrijkse Verzekering, Juris and La Mutuelle Patronale, is the country's sixth largest insurer with a market share of just over five percent.

AXA SA is the 11th largest insurer in the world with 131 billion French francs of consolidated revenues in 1995 and the eighth largest asset manager with 1,552 billion French francs of assets under management as of June 30 1996.
